A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison; all appendix pages match.

before.justification: v1 reports original CQL experiments on five Procgen games, with performance analyses in Figures 2–4 and numerical summaries in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original CQL experiments and empirical results in Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: The weighted target/source TD-error objective in Equation (10) and its CQL implementation are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Caveflyer, Climber, Dodgeball, Maze and Miner using the same source and target Procgen level scenarios.

E2.justification: The same CQL variants are compared across seven mixing weights, including target-only, equal mixing and source-only controls. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The reported level ranges, sample sizes, weight sweeps, model settings and hyperparameters are unchanged, including the 500 evaluation episodes specified in Table 5.

E4.justification: Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4 retain the same analyses of mixing weight, source–target discrepancy and target sample size. No additional ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting across mixing weights. No new information about repeated runs, seeds or uncertainty estimation is provided.

E6.justification: The plotted results, numerical entries and optimal-weight findings in Figures 2–4 and Tables 1–4 are unchanged. For example, Table 2's Maze result at N = 4000 remains 5.21 ± 0.69.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–2, Theorems 1–3, the optimal-weight derivations and all appendix proofs are unchanged. The appendix passage introducing a corrected version of Theorem 3 already appears in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, Main Contributions and Conclusion retain the same novelty claim, performance bounds, convergence guarantee and claims about optimal source–target weighting.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same bias–variance interpretation, qualifications about conservative bounds and difficult-to-estimate quantities, and distinction between minimizing the bound and optimizing actual performance.

D1.justification: The appendix implementation details, Table 5 hyperparameters and computing infrastructure are unchanged. Both versions still state that code will become available upon publication.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged, including the positioning relative to H2O, ORIS, DARC and DARA.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgments section after the Conclusion, identifying ONR support under contract N00014-23-1-2377, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The scientific prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2–4 have tighter row spacing, and page 7's text reflows to accommodate the acknowledgment. Table contents and captions are unchanged; all other pages match visually apart from the version stamp.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and makes small layout adjustments, while leaving the methods, evidence, interpretations, reproducibility information and appendix proofs unchanged. These administrative and presentation edits do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
